changes.comment: Open any local folder as a vault — pick a directory on the desktop app, or create one in the browser that survives a reload.
Keep several vaults and switch between them from a named list, with a settings panel alongside. Booting into a vault that has moved or gone unreadable now recovers instead of dead-ending.
Browse and reorganise a vault in a nested file tree: create, rename, move and delete files and folders, with a confirmation step in front of any change big enough to be a mistake.
Share a folder straight from the tree, by context menu or drag-and-drop, and mint, list or revoke its share tokens without leaving the app.
Join someone else’s shared folder as a mount inside your own vault, move files across the boundary, and fold the share back in when you are done.
Decide for yourself what happens to files that vanish underneath the app, in a review step, instead of having the choice made for you.
Find anything without leaving the keyboard — quick-open ordered by what you touched last, vault-wide search with snippets, and a command palette.
Follow wikilinks: click through them, autocomplete with `[[`, see unresolved links styled apart, and create the missing note by clicking it. Backlinks and outgoing-link panels show what points where.
Move back and forward through the files you have visited.
Choose a theme — two light/dark pairs, one of them a port of the Obsidian theme this replaces.
Forgetting a vault now clears its sync state too, so adding it back starts genuinely fresh.
Inspect what the sync layer is actually doing, in a devtools panel.
